messages:
mira: FYI we just got an RFP from BlueHarbor Bank — they want a capability matrix, security questionnaire answers, and a POC pricing sheet by EOW. Can someone own the tech responses?

sam: I can draft the capability matrix. need to confirm which features to call out (dedicated, private VPC, KMS/HSM, streaming, batching). Any special asks from procurement?

mira: Procurement wants pricing tiers for a 3-month POC and a production forecast (QPS + retention). Security wants SOC2 + network diagram and HSM options. They specifically asked about on-prem HSM integration and cross-region failover.

alex: For HSM we support customer-managed KMS and can integrate with HSMs via BYOK; for on-prem HSM we recommend Dedicated + Private control plane (see our deployment options). I'll write a short paragraph describing integration model.

jordan: I'll pull the template POC price sheet. Quick question: do we propose Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private for their compliance? Private if they need control plane in their VPC/on-prem. Dedicated if they want reserved GPU pools but still managed.

nina: BlueHarbor flagged latency SLOs (p99 < 250ms) for short responses (<128 tokens) and heavy embedding throughput for nightly indexing. We should recommend a Dedicated pool with autoscale and prefix caching to hit cost/latency targets.

sam: Draft capability matrix idea:
```
Feature | Supported | Notes
--- | --- | ---
Hosted API | Yes | Fast onboarding, usage pricing
Dedicated | Yes | Reserved GPU pools, SLA-backed
Private (VPC/on‑prem) | Yes | Customer-managed networking, HSM support
Streaming | Yes | gRPC/HTTP streaming
KV/prefix caching | Yes | Auto cache + manual hints
Quantization profiles | Yes | INT8/FP16, perf tradeoffs
Observability | Yes | Per-route traces, token cost heatmaps
Rollouts | Yes | Canary/A-B, auto-fallback
```

sam: I'll fill out rows and export to PDF.

mira: Flag: customer asked for an explicit statement on fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is exhausted. We need to confirm policy: do we auto-route to lower-tier model or queue?

alex: Current policy: by default we route to compatible hosted variant (model variant) on overflow; can be configured to queue or reject. I'll add exact language: "Smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or configured capacity tiers; customers may opt into queuing policies or strict rejection for cost control."

jordan: Legal asked for a list of attachments we plan to include when sending the RFP packet. Proposed attachments: SOC2 cert, Data Processing Addendum (DPA), example network diagram, POC price sheet, capability matrix PDF, HSM integration note, latency benchmark report. Any others?

nina: Add the standard security questionnaire answers file (we usually attach the completed encrypted Excel), and a sample SLAs doc for Dedicated.

mira: Can someone run a quick cost sketch for a 3-month POC: 2 Dedicated nodes (A100 equivalent), 500k embeddings/month, and 10M generated tokens/month? Need back-of-envelope so sales can propose commit levels today.

jordan: I'll run numbers and post in the thread in 30m.

deploy-bot: deploy: POC-price-template-v2.xlsx uploaded to #files by jordan (link: https://files.redwood/poc-price-template-v2.xlsx) :paperclip:

jordan: Uploaded the sketch: roughly $78k for 3 months with reserved capacity + embedding discounts baked in. I'll attach a breakdown in the packet.

sam: I'll merge the capability matrix with Alex's HSM paragraph and Nina's latency recommendations, then export.

mira: Great — aim to have the full packet (PDF + attachments) ready for internal review by tomorrow noon. I'll need a short executive summary (2–3 bullets) that highlights: compliance posture, recommended deployment, and POC acceptance criteria.

alex: I'll write the exec summary bullets.

nina: I'll pre-populate the security questionnaire answers and flag any open controls that need nuance.

mira: Thanks team. @jordan please send the internal draft to legal & security once it's assembled. I'll coordinate the final send to BlueHarbor. :thumbsup:

jordan: Will do.
